Target Business Services
Location: 61 Clifford Street, Maddington WA 6109 
Salary: $80,000 plus 12% superannuation
 
Our client Convenience Marketing Solutions Pty Ltd trading as Shikha Transport has been at the forefront of Western Australia’s heavy transport sector — has a story of growth, innovation and an unwavering commitment to clients’ success. The  vision is to be the most trusted and efficient bulk-haulage partner for the resources and agricultural sectors in WA, delivering every load safely, on time, and with the utmost professionalism. 

Shikha Transport operates a modern fleet including quad and super-quad trailer combinations to optimise payload and reduce vehicle movements. The services cover large-scale movement of iron ore, nickel, grain, sand and other essential raw materials, shuttle runs from mine sites to processing plants and ports, and timely agricultural haulage during peak harvest seasons. We provide integrated, end-to-end logistics solutions tailored to mining, construction and farming clients.

Shikha Transport is seeking full-time Truck Drivers experienced in heavy/bulk haulage to join its Maddington operations. These roles are vital to safely and efficiently moving high-volume bulk and palletised freight across WA, supporting production schedules, port transfers and construction/agricultural supply chains.

Essential requirements

-	AQF Certificate II or III in Driving Operations, or equivalent heavy vehicle qualification.
-	Minimum three years’ full-time experience in bulk haulage, multi-combination or heavy vehicle operations.
-	Valid MC (Multi Combination) driver licence (or applicable heavy vehicle licence for combination vehicles) with a clean driving history.
-	Demonstrated ability to safely operate quad / super-quad trailers and manage high-payload loads.
-	Familiarity with GPS, electronic logbook systems and modern fleet telematics.
-	Willingness to work flexible hours, including shift work, nights and occasional regional travel.

Key responsibilities are set out below: 

-	Safely operate heavy vehicles including quad and super-quad trailer combinations for bulk and palletised freight.
-	Perform shuttle runs, port transfers, site deliveries and bulk haulage for mining, agricultural and construction customers.
-	Load and unload cargo using appropriate equipment; secure loads in accordance with load-restraint requirements.
-	Conduct accurate pre-trip and post-trip inspections and complete vehicle defect reporting.
-	Maintain required driving and shift records (work diaries / electronic logbooks), fuel and mileage records.
-	Adhere to fatigue management rules, heavy vehicle regulations and Chain of Responsibility obligations.
-	Communicate proactively with dispatch and site personnel regarding ETAs, delays and site requirements.
-	Report vehicle faults and coordinate routine maintenance; assist with minor on-road repairs where safe and appropriate.
-	Uphold high standards of customer service and professional conduct at client sites.
-	Comply with site specific induction, safety and environmental protocols (PPE, permit to work, site inductions). 

Applications for this opportunity should be forwarded by email to: recruitment@targetbusiness.com.au 

Please note only short-listed candidates will be contacted and your application will be treated as strictly confidential.

Spark Easy Electrical Pty Ltd is a Sydney-based business specialising in solar panel installation, ducted air conditioning installation, and roof installation and restoration. The company is seeking an experienced Roof Tiler to support its roofing operations by installing, repairing and maintaining tiled roofing systems while ensuring high standards of workmanship and workplace safety. 

The successful applicant will be responsible for installing, repairing and maintaining tiled roofing systems while ensuring all work complies with Australian building standards and workplace safety requirements. This role is essential to maintaining the company's reputation for delivering high-quality roofing solutions and exceptional customer service. 

Minimum Requirements

-	Certificate III in Roof Tiling or an equivalent AQF qualification. 
-	At least two years of relevant full-time experience as a Roof Tiler. 
-	Demonstrated experience installing, repairing and restoring tiled roofs. 
-	Ability to safely work at heights and interpret roofing plans and specifications. 
-	Current White Card and a valid driver's licence. 

What you will be responsible for

-	Studying drawings, specifications and work sites to determine roofing materials and installation methods. 
-	Erecting ladders, scaffolding and fall-protection equipment in accordance with workplace safety requirements. 
-	Installing roofing underlay and securing waterproof sheets over eaves to protect roof structures. 
-	Aligning and fixing starter rows of roof tiles and laying successive rows to achieve correct alignment and weatherproof performance. 
-	Measuring, marking and cutting roof tiles to fit accurately around chimneys, valleys, skylights, vents, ridges and roof penetrations. 
-	Installing ridge and edge tiles using appropriate bedding mortar and pointing materials. 
-	Installing flashing and sealing roof penetrations to prevent water ingress. 
-	Inspecting roofs to identify damaged or defective tiles and carrying out repair and restoration work where required. 
-	Re-roofing existing buildings by removing damaged roofing materials and installing new tiled roofing systems. 
-	Applying sealants and flashing exposed nail heads and roof junctions to ensure long-term waterproofing. 
-	Maintaining roofing tools, equipment and materials in a safe and serviceable condition. 
-	Working collaboratively with supervisors and other construction trades to ensure projects are completed safely, efficiently and to specification. 
-	Ensuring all roofing work complies with Australian Standards, building regulations and workplace health and safety requirements. 

Skills, Experience and Attributes

-	Strong knowledge of roof tiling systems, roofing materials and installation techniques. 
-	Ability to read and interpret construction drawings and specifications. 
-	Excellent attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality workmanship. 
-	Strong problem-solving and organisational skills. 
-	Ability to work independently and as part of a team. 
-	Physically fit and capable of working safely at heights. 
-	Sound understanding of workplace health and safety requirements. 

The Successful Applicant

You will be required to work on residential and commercial roofing projects across Sydney. The position involves working outdoors in varying weather conditions, meeting project deadlines and maintaining high standards of workmanship and safety. You must demonstrate reliability, a strong work ethic, and the ability to communicate effectively with supervisors, clients and fellow tradespeople.

Please note only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and all applications will be treated as strictly confidential.

To apply for this position, email your resume to recruitment@targetbusiness.com.au.

Job description:

 
In collaboration with the Manager Outpatient Appointments and Theatre Booking Clerks, oversee, coordinate, and supervise all aspects of the day-to-day delivery of administrative and clerical functions in designated outpatient and outreach clinics including, reception, billing and provision of training and support for Team Leaders and Outpatient Appointment scheduling staff.

 

 






 

The Team

The Outpatient Operations team is part of the Outpatient Transformation Program, a statewide initiative focused on delivering efficient, patient-centred outpatient care. The team works across multiple hospitals and health sites to streamline administrative processes, improve referral and appointment management, and enhance communication with patients. By leveraging digital health solutions and modern workflows, the team ensures consistency, reduces missed appointments, and frees clinical staff to concentrate on direct patient care. Their work supports thousands of outpatient interactions daily, making them a critical link between patients, clinicians, and administrative systems.

The Role

In collaboration with the Manager Outpatient Appointments and Theatre Booking Clerks, oversee, coordinate, and supervise all aspects of the day-to-day delivery of administrative and clerical functions in designated outpatient and outreach clinics including, reception, billing and provision of training and support for Team Leaders and Outpatient Appointment scheduling staff.

Provide input, through operational analysis and recommendations, into administrative process improvements that support the management and integration of services into outpatient and remote outreach clinics.

Ensure the continuity and conformity of Outpatient Clinic standards and new administrative support services processes, by monitoring outcomes.

Develop, establish and maintain effective communication systems and collaborative relationships with stakeholders within THS to ensure the provision of timely flow of information and high-quality administrative services is provided by the administration team to the clinics.

You will need

In conjunction with the Team Leaders supervise and coordinate the work of the administration team, including managing leave and work rotations and ensuring priority tasks are completed within required timeframe.

Undertake a liaison role with senior medical and professional staff on, both routine and complex issues impacting on administrative matters to ensure operationally effective administrative support services are appropriate and negotiate and problem solve as required through interpretation of appropriate frameworks.

Provide leadership in the promotion, development, integration and implementation of quality improvement strategies for the effective and efficient delivery of administrative and clerical support services.

Why Tasmania

The Department of Health Tasmania oversees various hospitals across the state, including the Royal Hobart Hospital, Launceston General Hospital, Northwest Regional Hospital, and Mersey Community Hospital, as well as district hospitals and ambulance services. Additionally, it provides community health, mental health, and primary healthcare services to the Tasmanian community through more than 300 sites.

Tasmania, Australia's only island state, offers unparalleled natural beauty and a luxurious lifestyle. Pursuing your health career in Tasmania's public health system means building strong connections with colleagues and patients. It also means embracing a lifestyle where you can enjoy extraordinary experiences outside of work while making a significant impact on the community during work.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Transform lives, every single day

Do you want a career that means more? At Anglicare Sydney, we bring the strength, the support and the strategy to make it happen. 

For over 170 years, Anglicare has supported people and communities across Sydney and the surrounds. We are looking for a Workplace AI Product Owner to own and manage the Workplace AI product within our Digital and AI Enablement team.

The Workplace AI Product Owner is responsible for the end-to-end ownership of Anglicare's workplace AI product ecosystem. Operating within Digital and AI Enablement group of products, this role has organisation-wide reach and manages a growing portfolio of workplace AI capabilities, adoption pathways, enablement assets, governance processes, and approved automation scenarios that improve productivity, decision support, and staff effectiveness.

As part of a purpose-driven organisation, you will be working in a people-centred, collaborative, and values-led environment where your work directly contributes to enriching lives and strengthening communities.

Your opportunity

The Workplace AI Product Owner will maximise organisational value from workplace AI, by owning the systems, experiences, and enablement approaches that help staff adopt endorsed AI capabilities safely, practically, and at scale, continuously improving how workplace AI supports productivity, decision quality, and operational effectiveness through shared governance, insight, and product-led delivery.

With ownership, you will manage the following:

Product Ownership and Delivery

Translate the Workplace AI strategy and roadmap into prioritised initiatives, use cases, and delivery activities, ensuring the highest-value opportunities are progressed first.

Manage the full lifecycle of roadmap items with continual review, optimisation, and scaling of Workplace AI capabilities, while retiring or reshaping low-value approaches where appropriate.

Collaborate with delivery, architecture, and engineering teams to shape solutions that are valuable, usable, feasible, and scalable within the broader digital ecosystem.

Maintain an understanding of organisational priorities, workforce needs, AI market developments, and internal constraints to ensure the product evolves in line with strategic direction.

Adoption and Enablement

Design and deliver role-based adoption and enablement approaches, including training pathways, communities of practice, champions, practical playbooks, and targeted support materials.

Lead internal communications and engagement for Workplace AI, sharing practical guidance, success stories, updates, and use case examples that build awareness and confidence.

Establish fair and transparent prioritisation for rollout, licensing, and training so adoption is value-led, scalable, and equitable across teams

Identify user needs and pain points, using feedback and insight to continuously improve the workplace AI experience and increase sustained adoption.

Governance and Platform Enablement

Partner with business, technology, cyber, privacy teams to ensure Workplace AI use cases are safe, responsible, and aligned to enterprise governance requirements.

Enable approved automation and agent scenarios that extend Workplace AI outcomes, while working within enterprise guardrails and partnering with business owners for implementation and operational support.

Coordinate remediation plans for identified Workplace AI risks and findings with cyber and relevant 3rd party owners and support governance forums with clear reporting and decision material.

Build strong relationships across leadership, business, and technology teams to align stakeholders around priorities, investment choices, and responsible adoption.

Benefits Realisation and Insights

Define, measure, and report on Workplace AI product KPIs, adoption indicators, and benefit outcomes across personas and use cases.

Quantify how Workplace AI initiatives contribute to business outcomes such as time savings, improved quality, reduced cycle time, stronger decision support, and workforce effectiveness.

Use data, feedback, and experimentation to validate opportunities, inform prioritisation, and guide future investment decisions.

What you'll bring:

You will be equipped with the following skills.

Gen AI, automation or digital transformation initiatives

Product management (Agile, discovery-delivery)

Change management

Stakeholder engagement and communication

Technical fluency and systems thinking

Benefits realisation and performance measurement

You will also need:

Bachelor's degree in digital, technology, business, or a related field.

5+ years experience in product management, digital workplace, or a related role; or 1-2 years experience in gen AI enablement

Experience leading adoption, change, enablement, or capability uplift initiatives across diverse user groups.

Hands-on experience with Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Anthropic Claude

Why Anglicare?

At Anglicare, we provide meaningful opportunities and choice - both for the communities we support and the people who work with us. 

Here's what you'll enjoy: 

Flexible work options to balance life and career. 

Salary packaging benefits - up to $15,900 of your income tax free, plus $2,650 for meals and entertainment. 

Ongoing professional development and career pathways. 

Exclusive staff discounts with over 400 retailers. 

Employee Assistance Program and Fitness Passport with access to 800+ gyms. 

Belonging to a supportive, purpose-driven team committed to making a difference. 

Apply now

Are you ready to help us attract and empower the people who will shape Anglicare's future? To apply, click the 'Apply' button and submit your resum and cover letter. All applicants will receive a response. Anglicare is as wonderfully diverse as the communities we serve. While guided by our Christian values, our team includes people of all faiths and backgrounds.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Position Title: Post Graduate Fellow - Intensive Care Medicine
Employment Type: Temporary - 12 months with an option to extend 
Hours per week: 1.0 FTE (40 hours-week)
Position Grade: Post Graduate Fellow
Salary: As per the award
Enterprise Agreement: The Named NSW (Non-Declared) Affiliated Health Organisations' Staff Specialist Agreement 2021
Department Name: Intensive Care Medicine

About us: 
St Vincent's Hospital Sydney is a leading not-for-profit organisation providing health services to our community. Guided by our values of compassion, excellence, integrity and justice, we promote a culture of diversity and inclusion and empower our people to learn, grow and innovate.

Benefits of working at St Vincent's include:

Generous salary packaging and Fitness Passport for eligible staff

Opportunity to access a wide of range of clinical and non-clinical education programs

Supported post graduate opportunities within applicable fields

Career development opportunities across the St Vincent's Health Australia Network

Employee Assistance Program

Work-Life balance

About the role:

The Department of Intensive Care is seeking a Post Graduate Fellow to join our dynamic and highly motivated team, dedicated to providing state-of-the-art care to both the local community and patients referred from across New South Wales and beyond. 

At St Vincent's Hospital, Sydney, we strive to become the leading specialist intensive care unit in Australia for heart and lung disease, with a focus on cardio-pulmonary transplantation, mechanical cardiac support and extra-corporeal life support. We are constantly at the cutting edge of intensive care, through research, innovation, and collaboration. We endeavour to recruit and retain the highest quality staff, because it is through their skill and dedication that we as a department can continue to grow and develop.

As well as slotting seamlessly into the complex clinical duties of the role and actively engaging in governance, education and research, the successful candidate will be required to participate in the intensive care specialist on-call rotas, including critical care outreach and extra-corporeal support (eg. ECMO) retrieval.

Diversity and Inclusion at St Vincent's: 
St Vincent's is committed to employing a workforce that reflects the community we care for. We strongly encourage applications from people that are Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, culturally diverse, sexuality or gender diverse and-or living with disability.

Employment with St Vincent's is subject to you having current immunity status that complies with the Occupational Assessment, Screening & Vaccination against Specified Infectious Diseases - NSW Health Policy Directive (PD2023_022) or subsequent revisions in force. Appointment and ongoing employment will be subject to continued compliance with this policy directive.

Application Instructions: 
To have your application considered you are required to upload a current CV-Resume as well as a separate cover letter-document addressing the 'Selection Criteria' as below. Internal applicants i.e. current employees of St Vincent's Hospital or an entity of SVHA are required to apply via their Workday account.

Selection Criteria:

Possess, or be eligible to possess, specialist registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA), Fellowship of the College of Intensive Care Medicine (FCICM) of Australia and New Zealand, or equivalent.

Demonstrated knowledge, skills and high standards of clinical practice in Intensive Care Medicine commensurate to experience which is appropriate to the requirements of the position: possess experience in the management of critically ill and post-operative patients, including cardiopulmonary transplant, mechanical cardiac assist devices and extra-corporeal life support.

Significant experience in initiation and longitudinal management of extra-corporeal life support.

Experience and willingness to engage in the bedside application of echocardiography.

Demonstrated commitment to multidisciplinary education, with experience and training in high-fidelity simulation and its delivery in a critical care setting.

Ability to participate and lead clinical research projects.

Demonstrated leadership skills that support and foster innovation to create a learning culture, proven ability to improve the quality of services and patient care outcomes.

Demonstrated ability to provide high quality compassionate medical care as evidenced by recent practice experience in working congenially and collaboratively as both a leader and member of a multi-disciplinary team, and as a provider of services that engender high levels of patient satisfaction and experience. 

Personal integrity and demonstrated commitment to the Philosophy, Mission and Values of Mary Aikenhead Ministries and St Vincent's Health Australia

For more information, please contact Dr Hergen Buscher 

For a copy of the position description, please email svhs.smoadmin@svha.org.au

The closing date for application is 28 July 2026

To apply for this position, please click HERE    Click here to Apply now →

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Make a difference everyday

Join HammondCare and help improve quality of life for older Australians in need. As a not-for-profit, Christian organisation, we provide expert aged care, home care, dementia care and palliative care. Mission-led, we build passionate teams who support older people through life's most difficult circumstances.

With over 90 years of experience, we're known for our relationship-based approach. Whether it's in our homes, hospitals or the community, we bring skill, empathy and innovation to every moment of care. 

It's not just care. It's HammondCare.

Shape meaningful change. Support incredible people. Make an impact that matters every day.

Are you a passionate and adaptable HR professional who thrives in environments where no two days look the same? Do you enjoy partnering with leaders to create great employee experiences, solve complex people challenges, and help teams navigate change with confidence? If so-we'd love to meet you.

We're looking for a People Partner who wants to do more than just provide HR advice. In this role, you'll become a trusted coach, a steady guide through industry change, and a champion for the people who deliver exceptional care to older Australians.

This is a parental leave contract until 30 June 2027 based in St Leonards. The position has flexibility to be either 3 or 4 days per week (workload will be adjusted accordingly), with hybrid working options. 

What we can offer you

We care about your wellbeing at HammondCare and as a result offer a wide range of health and lifestyle benefits including: 

NFP salary packaging ($15,900 tax free) plus meals and entertainment benefit (up to $2,650 tax free)

Additional leave purchase options and 14 weeks paid parental leave

Flexible working options, including hybrid arrangements

Discounts on everyday products and services

Discounted healthcare memberships - access to network of fitness centres and pools for employees and families

Free independent, confidential counselling services, wellbeing resources and webinars available through our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family.

Health & Wellbeing programmes

Reward & Recognition programmes

Referral bonuses

Career and professional development opportunities

Why this role matters

Aged care is evolving rapidly-and so are the people needs within it. With ongoing regulatory reform, workforce shortages, shifting community expectations, and a diverse employee base, you'll play a critical role in helping our organisation stay ahead of the curve.

Your work will directly influence how our teams feel, grow, lead, and perform, ultimately shaping the experience of the residents and families we support.

What you'll be doing

Building strong partnerships with leaders to navigate a wide spectrum of people matters-from workforce planning and organisational change to culture, performance, and wellbeing

Supporting teams through sector-wide reform and regulatory updates, helping leaders translate requirements into practical people outcomes

Coaching leaders to build capability, resilience, and confidence in managing people

Streamlining people processes and identifying opportunities to improve the employee experience

Contributing to strategic people initiatives that uplift culture, engagement, and retention

What you'll bring

At least 5 year's demonstrated experience in HR, ideally in a complex, highly regulated or service-based environment (aged care or health experience a bonus but not essential)

A curious mindset-someone who asks questions, sees patterns, and anticipates what's coming next

Confidence in navigating challenging conversations with empathy and clarity

A collaborative, solutions-focused approach

A genuine passion for supporting a workforce that truly makes a difference

Why join us?

Work in a purpose-led organisation where your impact is felt immediately and meaningfully

Join a close-knit HR team that values collaboration, growth, and shared problem solving

Enjoy variety-every day brings a new challenge and a chance to learn

Be part of a sector undergoing positive transformation

If you are ready to make a difference with HammondCare, Apply Now! For any specific queries please contact talent@hammond.com.au.

Please indicate if you are looking for 3 or 4 days per week in your application.

Pre- Employment Checks 

All short-listed applicants will be asked to consent to a criminal record check and references.

HammondCare is committed to creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity and inclusion. We strive on creating an equal employment environment where everyone from any background can be themselves.    Click here to Apply now →

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Make a meaningful difference with us

We're looking for someone who wants to make the world a little better through small moments that leave big impacts. To build meaningful relationships and make a difference in the lives of others. 

Join us in driving meaningful change for First Nations children, young people,familiesand adults.

As theReconciliationActionPlan(RAP)Partner,you'lllead the coordination and delivery of key Reconciliation Action Plan(RAP)initiatives.You'llembed culturally informed practice and strengthen organisational capability across our services. 

This specialist roleprovidestrusted cultural advice to leaders,teamsand individuals.Working across programs,you'llhelp turn reconciliation commitments into real operational outcomes.Make a lasting impact in how we support First Nations communities every day.

Given the nature of the work and the requirement to provide cultural leadership and lived experience insights, it is a genuine occupational requirement under section 25 of theAnti-DiscriminationAct 1991 that the position be filled by an Aboriginal and-or Torres Strait Islander person.

Your part in our UnitingCare team:

Support the delivery of RAP priorities across UnitingCare Queensland, helping embed reconciliation commitments into everyday practice. 

Design and deliver practical, accessible learning and resources that build cultural capability and support respectful engagement with First Nations communities,clientsand Elders. 

Provide trusted, real-world cultural advice to teams, helping guide day-to-day decisions with confidence and care. 

Build andmaintainstrong, respectful relationships with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities,organisationsand Elders. 

Contribute to projects and service improvements, and provide clear, well-prepared reports,insightsand briefings to support leaders. 

Keep RAP activity runningsmoothlybycoordinatingreporting, tracking actions, supporting governancerequirementsand working closely withstakeholders

What makes a difference for us?

Tertiary qualifications ordemonstratedcompetency in Health and Community Services, plus the ability to obtain required probity checks (NDIS Worker Clearance, National Police Check). 

Experience building strong, respectful relationships with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and organisations. 

Ability to support a culturally safe workplace and build positive connections with First Nations staff. 

A good understanding of the history and current experiences of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and how this applies to service delivery. 

Strong communicationskills, with the ability to connect and build trust with a wide range of people. 

Clear and confident writing and digital skills, including creating practical resources,reportsand communications. 

Well organised and reliable, with the ability to manage admin, coordination and project work while keeping things running smoothly.

What makes a difference for you?

The opportunity to be part of the second-largest Queensland employer who has been leading by example for more than 100 years. Joining our team, you'll be welcomed as part of the UnitingCare family. We're a proud not-for-profit with more than 16,500 staff and 9,000 volunteers across our brands of BlueCare, Lifeline, ARRCS, The Wesley Hospital, Buderim Private Hospital, St Stephen's Hospital, and St Andrew's War Memorial Hospital.

Flexible work arrangements to support work-life balance

Access to salary packaging, meal and entertainment benefits - up to $15,900 per year tax free as well as up to $2,650 of your pre-tax income to pay for meal and entertainment benefits. To learn more about this benefit watch the video via the Salary Packaging Explained link

A recognition and rewards platform, providing employee discounts at hundreds of retailers, including everyday expenses, holidays, health insurance, annual awards celebration, wellbeing and employee assistance programs

12 weeks paid parental leave and 2 weeks paid partner leave, available after 6 months' service, in addition to the government scheme

Diversity and inclusive leave, offering paid gender affirmation leave and cultural leave options (paid and unpaid) for those who may celebrate Lunar New Year, Diwali, Ramadan, NAIDOC weeks and other significant cultural events

Career development opportunities to challenge yourself, grow and make a meaningful difference

A positive and inclusive team based on respect, shared standards, strong values and a commitment to serving others

Child safe, Child friendly 

UnitingCare is committed to being a Child Safe, Child Friendly organisation and will: 

provide welcoming, safe and nurturing services for children 

implement measures to prevent child abuse and neglect within our services 

appropriately and immediately address child abuse and neglect if it does occur 

abide by the Child Safe Standards and adhere to the Reportable Conduct Scheme 

Diversity & Inclusion 

Our approach is simple - everybody is welcome here. At UnitingCare, diversity is at the core of our who we are, our mission and our values. We are committed to providing equal opportunities to all employees no matter their sex, race, culture, sexual orientation, disability or gender identity. Demonstrating our commitment to reconciliation and building long-term employment opportunities for First Nations peoples, UnitingCare strongly encourages Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants for this position. 

Safe workplace 

We work hard to make our services welcoming and safe for every person. We are united in keeping children, young people and the elderly safe from harm, within our services, workplaces and the communities we support. We are committed to speaking up loudly for their safety.

Commitment to Safeguarding

We are committed in creating services and workplaces that are welcoming and safe for every person. We work together to protect children, young people, adults and the elderly from harm within our services and the communities we support. We speak up for their safety to ensure their voices are heard. Our recruitment and workplace practices reflect our dedication in preventing abuse, harm and exploitation across UnitingCare.    Click here to Apply now →

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Transform lives, every single day 

Do you want a career that means more? At Anglicare Sydney, we bring the strength, support and strategy to make it happen.

We are a well-respected not-for-profitthat'sbeen servingsociety'smost vulnerable for more than 170 years. Each year, we achieve life-changing outcomes for the 40,000+ people who rely on our person-centeredsupport. And now,we'reextending our reach and impact even further.

As aMaintenance Officer, you'll play a vital role in ensuring our residents enjoy a safe, comfortable and well-maintained environment. Through your practical skills and commitment to service excellence, you'll help create a community where residents feel supported, valued and proud to call home.

Join a collaborative and values-driven team where respect, integrity and quality are at the heart of everything we do.

Your Opportunity

This is apart-time opportunity based atWooloowareShores, Taren Point, working Sunday to Wednesday from 8:00am to 4:00pm.

As aMaintenance Officer,you will be responsible for carrying out general maintenance, repairs and preventative maintenance activities across the village. Working closely with residents, contractors and village teams, you will ensure buildings, grounds and facilities are maintained to a high standard while delivering excellent customer service.

With professionalism, initiative and a commitment to quality, you will:

Maintenance & Service Delivery

Complete a range of maintenance tasks safely and efficiently, including repairs, painting, minor building works and general handyman duties

Carry out preventative maintenance programs to ensure facilities and equipment remain in excellent condition

Conduct fault finding and minor repairs to appliances and village assets

Maintain buildings, grounds and common areas to a high standard

Ensure tools and equipment are maintained and used safely

Identify maintenance issues proactively and recommend repairs or replacement works where required

Resident Support & Customer Service

Provide courteous and professional service to residents, visitors and contractors

Support residents with maintenance-related requests while respecting their dignity and privacy

Build positive relationships and contribute to a welcoming village environment

Uphold Anglicare's values through all interactions

Administration & Compliance

Maintain accurate maintenance records and documentation

Ensure work is completed in accordance with organisational policies and procedures

Support after-hours maintenance requirements when required, with time in lieu provided

Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance service delivery

Safety & Workplace Culture

Follow all workplace health and safety requirements and safe work practices

Report hazards, incidents and risks in accordance with organisational processes

Maintain a clean, safe and organised work environment

Contribute to a respectful and inclusive workplace culture

What You'll Bring

You are practical, reliable and customer-focused, with a genuine commitment to providing excellent service and maintaining high standards.

You will also need:

Experience in general building maintenance, handyman services or a related trade environment

Basic knowledge of building maintenance, repairs and equipment

Strong problem-solving skills and practical approach to maintenance tasks

Ability to prioritise work and manage multiple responsibilities

Good communication and customer service skills

Computer skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook

Current NSWDriver's Licence, good to have 

Desirable

Certificate or qualification in maintenance, building services or a related field

Experience working within retirement living, aged care or hospitality environments

You will thrive in this role if you are:

Hands-on and solutions focused

Organised and able to work independently

Calm under pressure and adaptable to changing priorities

Committed to delivering high-quality workmanship

Passionate about supporting older Australians

Why Anglicare? 

We provide meaningful opportunities and choice, both for the individuals and communities we support, and the dedicated people here who make it happen. 

At Anglicare, you'll get the security, stability and opportunities that come with a strong, well-established organisation that's ready for the future. You'll belong to a community of kind, humble, and respectful people of all faiths and backgrounds. You will also be supported to gain new knowledge, deepen your experience and expertise, and shape a rewarding career.
